files.why: Framework-free identity vocabulary: a Role union including "finance" and a CurrentUser entity.
Pure reusable predicate (e.g. hasRole(user, role)) with no framework deps, mirroring other slices' core/policy.ts.
Zod DTO for the current-user endpoint response, kept private to data/ like billing's dto.ts.
Maps the current-user DTO to the CurrentUser core entity so DTOs never leak upward.
fetchCurrentUser() over @shared/http/transport with zod validation, following the data-layer pattern.
MSW handler serving a mock current user + role, since there is no real auth backend today.
Pinia cache for the reactive current-user session shared across views (a cache-with-IO belongs in data/, not shared/).
Public reactive accessor exposing the current user/role to consumers; also satisfies the required ui/ folder.
Required 5th slice entry (empty route list — identity renders no pages); index must re-export it.
The slice's only public surface: Role type, useCurrentUser, mock handlers, routes.
canVoid must also require void authority (add a role/authority param); stays pure and framework-free.
Read the current role via the @slices/identity public alias and feed it into canVoid so canVoidInvoice reflects the finance gate.
Existing canVoid tests must be updated for the new finance-authority signature (currently assert only status).
Compose the identity slice's mock handlers into the MSW worker (composition-root concern).
Concatenate identityRoutes to keep the router's slice-route composition complete (empty set today).
Register "identity" in the slices array so the toolchain/allow-list follows; CODEOWNERS-protected, needs architecture review.
Regenerated from architecture.config.ts to add the new slice's per-folder import rules (not hand-edited).
Regenerated allow-list that legalizes the billing→identity edge via index.ts (not hand-edited).

uncertain: Biggest one: whether identity belongs in a NEW slice vs a session helper in shared/. "user"/"role"/"finance" are not in domainNouns so shared/ wouldn't trip the grep-test, but a stateful cache-with-an-IO-habit is explicitly not a shared/ primitive (per store.ts's own comment) — I lean toward a slice, but this is a real judgment call.
Slice name: identity vs access vs auth vs session — picked "identity" arbitrarily.

How the role reaches billing/core/policy.ts: pass a plain boolean authority, pass a Role value, or import identity's Role type into billing/core. I lean toward passing a boolean/value so billing/core stays ignorant of identity's vocabulary and avoids any cross-slice coupling in the most stable layer.

Whether InvoiceDetailView.vue changes at all: folding the role check into the existing canVoidInvoice computed means the view needs NO edit; a separate disabled/explained button for non-finance users would require modifying it.
Whether router/index.ts should wire identityRoutes given the route list is empty today (may be unnecessary).
questions: Where does the role actually come from — a real auth/session/JWT endpoint, or is a mocked current-user (MSW only) the expectation for now?

This adds a slice, which edits CODEOWNERS-protected files (architecture.config.ts + the generated configs) and requires architecture review. Is that acceptable, or is there an approved/intended home for identity I'm missing?
Should voiding also be enforced server-side (the voidInvoice mutation), or is hiding the button UI-only for now? UI gating alone is not a security boundary.
Role model: a single "finance" role, or a set of roles/permissions? Are there other roles in play today?
For non-finance users: hide the button entirely (as requested), or show it disabled with an explanation?
